author: reek
body: StringBuilder is a mutable record and sb-append writes its parts in place, so handing one builder to two owners would let each believe it holds the builder alone. Here the builder arrives as a declared parameter and is appended to twice on one path, which is aliasing, and the compiler must refuse it.

author: reek
body: This pins the protection rather than the defect. sb-append threads the record onward, so the checker treats it as consuming; were the signature ever changed so that it merely borrowed, the aliasing above would start compiling and the in-place append would corrupt both results with nothing to say so.

author: reek
body: The local-bound-from-a-call half of the same aliasing is caught too, since the minted-mutable walk; its pin is the sibling test stringbuilder-alias-local. Together the two hold both ways a builder can arrive.
